objective.statement: Build the scales of G major and D major by raising notes with sharps.
successCriteria: I know a new key starts on a different note but uses the same pattern.
I know G major needs F sharp and D major needs F sharp and C sharp.
I can write both scales with the right accidentals.

explanation.text: If we start a major scale on G and use only white keys, the pattern goes wrong: the last step is a tone instead of a semitone. To fix it, the 7th note must be raised to F sharp.

music.textAlternative: The scale of G major in the treble clef: G A B C D E F sharp G.

explanation.caption: G major: G A B C D E F♯ G. One sharp, on the 7th note.

explanation.text: D major starts on D. To keep the pattern we need two sharps: F sharp and C sharp.

music.textAlternative: The scale of D major in the treble clef: D E F sharp G A B C sharp D.

explanation.caption: D major: D E F♯ G A B C♯ D. Sharps on the 3rd and 7th notes.

explanation.text: Notice every letter name is used once, in order. We write F♯, never G♭, because the scale would then skip F and use G twice.
After writing a scale, check the pattern: semitones come between notes 3-4 and 7-8.

music.textAlternative: The scale of G major with F sharp as the 7th note, each note linked to its key.

steps: Tap the notes from G upwards. The 7th note, F sharp, is a black key.
Compare with F natural: the step up to G would be a tone, not a semitone.
F sharp makes the last step a semitone, as the pattern needs.
demonstration.textAlternative: The scale of G major, with F sharp as the 7th note, each linked to its keyboard key.

guided.prompt: This is the scale of G major, going up. One note is missing and is shown as a rest. Which note belongs in the gap?

hints: Tone, tone, semitone, tone, tone, tone, semitone.

feedback.correct: F♯ is the note G major needs.

mistakes.semitone-misplaced: Check the pattern of tones and semitones — the semitones aren't where they belong.
mistakes.letter-skipped-or-repeated: Each letter name appears once. You've used one letter twice and skipped another — respell that note.
mistakes.wrong-minor-form: Check which form of the minor scale is asked for, and which notes that form changes.
mistakes.melodic-descent-not-restored: Coming down, the melodic minor uses the notes of the key signature — undo the raised 6th and 7th.
mistakes.key-signature-misapplied: With a key signature, notes it covers don't need accidentals. Without one, every sharp or flat must be written.
mistakes.wrong-direction-or-octave: Check whether the question asks for ascending or descending, and which octave to start on.

feedback.fallback: Not quite. Write one note per letter name first, then check the tones and semitones.
